text:
maria: Heads up — drift detector fired for eu-west allocator parity. CI reported different planned node counts vs live.

devon: saw that. plan shows 4 g4dn pools, live has 6. autoscaler config looks different (min/desired).

li: I ran a gitops-diff: `flux diff --namespace infra --source=git` — it flagged helm release `allocator` values changed in cluster (image tag + minNodes).

samir: OPA policy also blocked a reconcile earlier today on networkpolicy/ingress-eu. Could that gate have stopped the automated fix?

ops-bot: [AUTO] drift-detector: allocator/production-eu mismatch: terraform=4 nodes, cluster=6 nodes, last-applied=1755551200. Severity=medium.

maria: yes, the reconcile was queued but OPA deny prevented the Helm hook that would have patched minNodes. The hook requires the networkpolicy to be in place first.

devon: quick plan of attack: 1) bisection to find when minNodes diverged (terraform state vs gitops). 2) run `terraform plan -target=module.alloc` in staging to confirm parity. 3) if mismatch root is manual patch, revert and open change through git.

li: I started the bisection: `scripts/bisect-env-diff --service allocator --from=1750000000 --to=1755554321`. Found the change: manual kubectl patch on 1755432100 by user: oncall-ops — message "temp bump for training run".

samir: That explains the burst. Cost alert was triggered last night. We need a remediation that doesn't cause churn. Suggest turning on `reconcile.forcePatch=false` and create a canary PR that adjusts autoscaler profile and adds a short ttl to the manual override annotation.

maria: Agree. Also, add a preflight check in the gitops pipeline: fail if cluster and terraform diverge more than 10% on node counts for GPU pools.

devon: I've drafted a quick PR: `infra/profiles/allocator-eu.yml` — changes: restore minNodes to 4, add annotation `redwood.io/manual-override: expires=1755580000`, add helm test to assert networkpolicy present before allocating gpus.

li: Can we also add a lightweight remediation runbook to the thread? Something like: 
```
- detect drift (drift-detector alerts)
- run bisect script to identify manual overrides
- if manual override found: annotate with expiry and notify owner, create PR to reconcile
- if no override: run terraform apply targeting allocator after approval
- post-reconcile: monitor cost & pod evictions for 1 hour
```

samir: +1. I'll add an OpsRun link and schedule a small canary deploy window (20m) to avoid disrupting training jobs.

maria: I'll notify finance about the temporary cost spike and mark this incident as low-impact since no pod evictions occurred.

devon: ops-bot, kick a dry-run reconcile after PR merges?

ops-bot: [ACTION] Will run `flux reconcile` dry-run for allocator once PR merged and report back as a thread reply.

maria: Thanks. Closing loop — once the dry-run is clean, we merge, then watch logs for autoscaler thrash.

li: note: we should add a periodic parity scan every 6h and alert only when >10% delta for GPU pools to reduce noise.

samir: I'll create the alert change ticket. tagging @oncall for visibility. :bell:

maria: great work — small follow-ups: add ttl annotation parser to reconciliation controller and update runbook.

devon: filing the infra PR now.
